title: Property of a Female Hindu to be Her Absolute Property — Section 14 HSA

content.overview: Section 14 of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956 converts limited estate of a female Hindu into absolute ownership. Any property possessed by a female Hindu, whether acquired before or after the commencement of the Act, shall be held by her as full owner and not as a limited owner, subject to the proviso for property acquired under a gift, will, or other instrument / decree / order / award prescribing a restricted estate.
content.glance: Ask: (1) Female Hindu? (2) Property possessed? (3) Absolute ownership under s. 14(1)? (4) Restricted estate under proviso to s. 14(2)?
content.study:
Section 14(1): any property possessed by a female Hindu, whether acquired before or after the commencement of the Act, shall be held by her as full owner thereof and not as a limited owner.

Explanation clarifies that ‘property’ includes both movable and immovable property acquired by inheritance, partition, gift, purchase, prescription, or in any other manner, and also includes stridhana.

Section 14(2): nothing in sub-section (1) applies to any property acquired by gift, will, or under any other instrument, or under a decree or order of a civil court, or under an award, where the terms prescribe a restricted estate.

Core effect: the old limited woman’s estate is enlarged to absolute ownership where s. 14(1) applies. s. 14(2) preserves intentionally created restricted estates.

No case holdings invented. Case-law verification remains a separate gate.

sections.heading: Absolute ownership under s. 14(1)
sections.body: Property possessed by a female Hindu is held as full owner, not limited owner.

sections.heading: Wide meaning of property
sections.body: Includes movable and immovable property from inheritance, partition, gift, purchase, prescription, and stridhana.

sections.heading: Restricted estate exception — s. 14(2)
sections.body: Gift, will, instrument, decree, order or award prescribing a restricted estate is not enlarged by s. 14(1).

sections.heading: Possessed
sections.body: Possession (actual or constructive as required by the statutory scheme) is the gateway to enlargement under s. 14(1).

sections.heading: Effect on succession
sections.body: Once absolute, the property devolves on her intestacy under ss. 15–16, not under the old limited-estate reversion rules.

provisions.title: Property of a female Hindu to be her absolute property

examples.title: Limited estate enlarged
examples.body: Female Hindu possessed of property as limited owner at commencement — holds as full owner under s. 14(1) if s. 14(2) does not apply.

examples.title: Restricted gift preserved
examples.body: Gift deed expressly creates a life interest only — s. 14(2) prevents enlargement to absolute ownership.

hypotheticals.question: Does every female’s property become absolute under s. 14?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. s. 14(2) preserves restricted estates created by gift, will, instrument, decree, order or award.

misconceptions.trap: s. 14 abolishes all restricted estates for Hindu females.
misconceptions.correction: s. 14(2) expressly preserves restricted estates created by the listed instruments.

enhancement.definition: Section 14 HSA converts limited estate of a female Hindu into absolute ownership of property possessed by her, subject to the restricted-estate proviso.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Possessed property is held as full owner under s. 14(1) unless s. 14(2) preserves a restricted estate.
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Statutory enlargement of woman’s estate with a clear exception for intentional restrictions.
